documents.title: Generative AI Syllabus Statement Considerations
tiers: No use of generative AI permitted
Use permitted under some circumstances or with explicit permission
documents.summary: CTE guidance that recommends a hybrid: a minimum syllabus requirement tied to the Aggie Honor Code plus instructor-set expectations. It supplies borrowed sample syllabus statements at three permission levels, from no AI to broad use with citation.
documents.stance_why: The document does not set a university-wide rule on AI; it recommends a hybrid in which instructors "establish clear expectations" and offers sample statements grouped by three permission levels, so stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The opening sentence says the university wishes to approach generative AI "with scholarly rigor, intellectual integrity, and educational excellence"; it sets institution-wide purpose and principles, so P56, informs, general.
units.anchor: with scholarly rigor, intellectual integrity, and educational excellence

units.why: States AI offers "stimulating opportunities to educate effectively for the future of learning and work", a future-readiness reason to engage with AI, so P44 rather than P87 (which excludes career claims).
units.anchor: stimulating opportunities to educate effectively for the future of learning and work
units.fit_note: Also names academic-integrity challenges, not only opportunities.

units.why: The recommended option adds a minimum syllabus requirement that makes explicit the "responsibility of instructors and students to establish clear expectations" in each course or assignment; this is the syllabus-statement requirement (P09), not P04 because it mandates stating expectations.
units.anchor: responsibility of instructors and students to establish clear expectations for generative AI use
units.policy: The recommended hybrid adds a minimum syllabus requirement making explicit the responsibility of instructors and students to establish clear expectations for generative AI use within each course and/or assignment.

units.why: The recommended course of action pairs a university-level syllabus requirement with individual instructor determinations (option 2: "allow individual instructors to determine their own syllabus statement"); this assigns the decision on acceptable use to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: (Recommended) Pursue a hybrid of the two previous options
units.policy: The recommended approach for the institution is a hybrid of a university-wide minimum syllabus requirement and individual instructors determining acceptable generative AI use in their own courses.
units.fit_note: Hybrid: university sets a minimum syllabus requirement and instructors decide the actual rule.

units.why: The syllabus requirement "reinforces that the use of generative AI in academic coursework is integrally related to academic integrity and will be governed by the Aggie Honor Code"; this classifies AI use under the integrity code (P36).
units.anchor: will be governed by the Aggie Honor Code
units.policy: Use of generative AI in academic coursework is integrally related to academic integrity and will be governed by the Aggie Honor Code.

units.why: The hybrid includes "Guidance provided to support faculty in making their individual determinations"; support for faculty deciding AI policy fits P63.
units.anchor: Guidance provided to support faculty in making their individual determinations

units.why: The document organizes sample statements into three permission levels (no use; some circumstances or explicit permission; broader use within guidelines), i.e. named tiers of AI use, so P05.
units.anchor: Sample Syllabus Statements Grouped by Permission Level

units.why: Clarifies that the sample statements are instructors' own syllabus language, not institutional policy; this scopes what the samples mean, closest to P61 (scope).
units.anchor: The samples represent instructor uses on their own syllabi and not institutional policies.
units.fit_note: Scope note about the status of the samples rather than a definition of AI.

units.why: Sample (Bryant) statement bans AI writing tools "for any stage or phase of work": a default ban on all work, P01.
units.anchor: AI Writing tools are not permitted for any stage or phase of work

units.why: Sample (Bryant): using the tools "would be considered academically dishonest"; classifies prohibited AI use as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: your actions would be considered academically dishonest and a violation of Bryant

units.why: Sample (Princeton): "All work submitted in this course must be your own"; students own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: All work submitted in this course must be your own

units.why: Sample (Princeton) bars use of ChatGPT or other AI composition software outright: P01.
units.anchor: You may not engage in unauthorized collaboration or make use of ChatGPT

units.why: Sample (Texas Tech): because writing and thinking skills are learning outcomes, "all writing assignments should be prepared by the student"; the student must produce the submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: all writing assignments should be prepared by the student

units.why: Sample (Texas Tech) gives "prepare you for a competitive workplace" as the reason to do writing without AI: a career reason for building skills without AI, P94.
units.anchor: Developing strong competencies in this area will prepare you for a competitive workplace

units.why: Sample (Texas Tech): AI-generated submissions "will be treated as plagiarism", classifying them as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: AI-generated submissions are not permitted and will be treated as plagiarism

units.why: Sample (UNH): "Unless otherwise specified" AI tools are strictly prohibited "even when properly attributed"; this states the fallback when the instructor specifies nothing, P06.
units.anchor: Unless otherwise specified, the use of Automated Writing Tools
units.policy: Unless otherwise specified, use of automated writing tools including ChatGPT and similar AI tools is strictly prohibited in the course, even when properly attributed.

units.why: Sample (UNH): use "is considered plagiarism" and handled under existing policy; P36.
units.anchor: The use of automated writing tools is considered plagiarism

units.why: Sample (UC Irvine writing class): work "will be generated by the students themselves" and having AI like ChatGPT write a substantial portion is an integrity violation; P19.
units.anchor: will be generated by the students themselves
units.policy: Students submit work generated by themselves; having another person or entity, including AI affordances like ChatGPT, write any substantive portion of an assignment is an academic-integrity violation.

units.why: Sample (Bryant, some circumstances): AI use is allowed only where the instructor says when, where and how, i.e. decided per activity, P04.
units.anchor: You will be informed as to when, where, and how these tools are permitted

units.why: Sample (Bryant): use outside the permission "constitutes a violation"; unauthorized use is misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Any use outside of this permission constitutes a violation of Bryant

units.why: Sample (Bryant): AI is "not a replacement for human creativity, originality, and critical thinking"; student remains the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: AI programs are not a replacement for human creativity, originality, and critical thinking

units.why: Sample (Bryant): AI may be used "within limited circumstances, and with proper attribution"; permitted with attribution, P24.
units.anchor: within limited circumstances, and with proper attribution, AI programs may be used as a tool
units.fit_note: Also limits use to limited circumstances.

units.why: Sample (Princeton, some circumstances): "must obtain permission from me before using AI composition software"; AI is off unless the instructor permits, P01 (ban unless permitted).
units.anchor: Students must obtain permission from me before using AI composition software
units.fit_note: Ban lifted by instructor permission rather than an absolute ban.

units.why: Sample (UNH): if permitted, AI tools "should be used with caution and proper citation"; citation requirement, P24.
units.anchor: should be used with caution and proper citation

units.why: Sample (UNH): "AI is not a replacement for your own thinking and research"; students stay the primary thinker, P32.
units.anchor: AI is not a replacement for your own thinking and research

units.why: Sample (WashU): using an AI generator "without proper attribution or authorization is a form of academic dishonesty"; misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: without proper attribution or authorization is a form of academic dishonesty

units.why: Sample (WashU): "If you are unsure ... please contact your instructor"; ask when unsure, P10.
units.anchor: please contact your instructor to discuss the issue

units.why: Sample (Colorado): "you will be asked to use AI tools to explore how they can be used" in the course; AI use built into some activities, P79.
units.anchor: you will be asked to use AI tools to explore how they can be used

units.why: Sample (Colorado): outside designated tasks students "are discouraged from using AI tools to generate content"; discouraged not forbidden, P03.
units.anchor: you are discouraged from using AI tools to generate content

units.why: Sample (Colorado): work using AI "should clearly indicate what work is the student's work and what part is generated by the AI"; disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: Any student work submitted using AI tools should clearly indicate what work

units.why: Sample (Colorado): "no more than 25% of the student work should be generated by AI"; AI content allowed under a percentage cap, P16.
units.anchor: no more than 25% of the student work should be generated by AI
units.fit_note: The sample concerns text, video, audio and images, not specifically code.

units.why: Sample (Colorado): if unclear, "reach out to me for a conversation before submitting"; ask first, P10.
units.anchor: please reach out to me for a conversation before submitting your work

units.why: Sample (Bryant, broader use): AI tools "are welcome ... provided that you cite when and how you use the tool"; default permit with citation, P02.
units.anchor: AI Writing tools such as ChatGPT are welcome in this class, provided that you cite

units.why: The sample attribution language names the tool and model ("GPT-3, OpenAI's large-scale language-generation model"), an example of citation naming the tool; P25.
units.anchor: The author generated this text in part with GPT-3

units.why: The Bryant sample attribution says the author "takes ultimate responsibility for the content"; students own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: takes ultimate responsibility for the content of this publication

units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst): "students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work"; cite AI use, P24.
units.anchor: students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work

units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst): generating content "without proper attribution qualifies as academic dishonesty"; non-disclosure is itself the violation, P28.
units.anchor: without proper attribution qualiﬁes as academic dishonesty

units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst, encouraged): students "can choose to use AI tools to help brainstorm"; brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: You can choose to use AI tools to help brainstorm assignments or projects

units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst, encouraged): AI may be used "to revise existing work you have written"; editing support, P91.
units.anchor: or to revise existing work you have written

units.why: Sample (UMass Amherst): "I expect you to clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool" e.g. a different font colour; marking AI text where used, P24.
units.anchor: clearly attribute what text was generated by the AI tool
units.fit_note: Marks AI-generated text in place, e.g. different colored font or parenthetical.

units.why: Sample (Iowa): students "should indicate ... how you validated any AI-generated citations, which may be invented by the AI"; verify output, P31.
units.anchor: how you validated any AI-generated citations, which may be invented by the AI

units.why: Sample (Iowa): "Assignment guidelines will provide additional guidance"; assignment-level rules, P04.
units.anchor: Assignment guidelines will provide additional guidance as to how these tools

units.why: Sample (Iowa, encouraged): students "are invited to use AI platforms to help prepare for assignments" e.g. brainstorming; P15.
units.anchor: Students are invited to use AI platforms to help prepare for assignments and projects

units.why: Sample (Iowa, encouraged): "welcome you to use AI tools to help revise and edit your work"; editing support, P91.
units.anchor: I also welcome you to use AI tools to help revise and edit your work

units.why: Sample (Iowa): AI-generated essay parts appear in a different colour and the relationship to student work "should be discussed in cover letters"; reflection submitted with work, P26.
units.anchor: the relationship between those sections and student contributions should be discussed in cover letters

documents.unit: Texas A&M AI initiative / Division of Academic Affairs
documents.title: Use Guidelines and Ethics (Teach with AI)
documents.summary: University AI site page of ethical principles and role-specific best practices for faculty, staff and students. It leaves course rules to instructors while setting expectations on citation, privacy, verification and approved tools.
documents.stance_why: The page gives recommendations, not a single rule: it says "The faculty should provide clear instructions about permissible AI uses in their courses" and students should "Check for AI-related policies set by your instructor"; it welcomes AI use generally but leaves course rules to instructors.

units.why: The purpose statement says the page provides "recommendations and guidance on the responsible use of generative AI" to maximize benefits and minimize risks; framework and purpose, P56.
units.anchor: recommendations and guidance on the responsible use of generative AI

units.why: "Generative AI use ... should adhere to the same ethical principles ... privacy, fairness, transparency, bias, and accountability"; institution-wide principles, P56.
units.anchor: should adhere to the same ethical principles used in other aspects of education

units.why: "We must ensure that we implement algorithms that incorporate fairness measures and conduct routine audits to detect and address prejudices"; auditing AI systems for bias, P98.
units.anchor: conduct routine audits to detect and address prejudices

units.why: "Everyone should ensure the AI systems are transparent and explainable to professors and students"; system transparency, nearest P98.
units.anchor: AI systems are transparent and explainable to professors and students
units.fit_note: Concerns explainability of AI systems to users rather than audit or monitoring.

units.why: "Everyone must follow data privacy and security guidelines ... protecting personal and institutional data"; P50.
units.anchor: Everyone must follow data privacy and security guidelines when using generative AI

units.why: Explains that platforms "may collect, store, and process personal data, potentially leading to privacy risks"; data privacy rationale, P50.
units.anchor: these platforms may collect, store, and process personal data

units.why: "The use of copyrighted materials to train generative AI models must respect these rights"; copyright, P52.
units.anchor: use of copyrighted materials to train generative AI models must respect these rights

units.why: Transparency: "clearly documenting the use of AI-generated content, properly attributing AI-assisted contributions in research and academic work"; disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: properly attributing AI-assisted contributions in research and academic work

units.why: Transparency principle: implementation of AI tools "aligns with the University's policies and broader ethical standards"; compliance with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: ensuring that the implementation of such tools aligns with the University

units.why: "users must acknowledge the use of nontrivial AI-generated content and avoid plagiarism"; disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: users must acknowledge the use of nontrivial AI-generated content and avoid plagiarism
units.fit_note: Threshold: only nontrivial AI-generated content must be acknowledged.

units.why: "It is permissible to use AI for correcting spelling and grammar and for formatting references"; editing permission, P91.
units.anchor: permissible to use AI for correcting spelling and grammar and for formatting references

units.why: Same sentence limits permitted uses: "but not for generating new text"; do not have AI produce submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: but not for generating new text

units.why: "The faculty should provide clear instructions about permissible AI uses in their courses"; communicate expectations, P09.
units.anchor: The faculty should provide clear instructions about permissible AI uses in their courses

units.why: Faculty instructions "should include specific guidance on academic integrity policies related to AI tools"; P09.
units.anchor: This should include specific guidance on academic integrity policies related to AI tools
units.fit_note: Adds that the instructions include integrity-policy guidance.

units.why: Names bias harms: "Biases in training data or algorithms lead to distorted and potentially harmful outcomes"; P53.
units.anchor: Biases in training data or algorithms lead to distorted and potentially harmful outcomes

units.why: "Faculty, students, and staff must hold themselves accountable for the decisions and actions taken by the AI systems that they choose to use"; ownership, P29.
units.anchor: must hold themselves accountable for the decisions and actions taken by the AI systems

units.why: "Users are also responsible for reviewing the accuracy of any output"; verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Users are also responsible for reviewing the accuracy of any output they generate

units.why: "Non-compliance ... may result in disciplinary action, including academic penalties or loss of access to AI tools and services"; sanctions named, P37.
units.anchor: may result in disciplinary action, including academic penalties or loss of access to AI tools
units.fit_note: Penalties are listed only generally, not specific amounts.

units.why: "Users should report violations to the appropriate authorities"; duty to report violations by others, P71.
units.anchor: Users should report violations to the appropriate authorities at Texas A&M University

units.why: Under Teach: "Use generative AI to enhance teaching and learning experiences while maintaining academic integrity"; welcomes AI use, P02.
units.anchor: Use generative AI to enhance teaching and learning experiences while maintaining academic integrity

units.why: "Be transparent about the use of AI-generated content in course materials"; P48.
units.anchor: Be transparent about the use of AI-generated content in course materials

units.why: "Encourage students to use AI responsibly and ethically"; encourages student AI use, P02.
units.anchor: Encourage students to use AI responsibly and ethically

units.why: "Update syllabi to reflect policies on AI use in coursework"; P09.
units.anchor: Update syllabi to reflect policies on AI use in coursework

units.why: "Consider integrating AI purposefully into teaching, such as assignments that prepare students for AI interactions in their future careers"; career skill, P44.
units.anchor: integrating AI purposefully into teaching, such as assignments that prepare students for AI interactions

units.why: Under Learn: "Use generative AI to support learning and research while adhering to academic integrity policies"; P02.
units.anchor: Use generative AI to support learning and research while adhering to academic integrity policies

units.why: "Properly cite AI-generated content in academic work"; P24.
units.anchor: Properly cite AI-generated content in academic work

units.why: "Be aware of the limitations of AI-generated content and verify its accuracy before using it"; P31.
units.anchor: verify its accuracy before using it in academic or research contexts

units.why: Research bullet: use AI for idea development and design "while maintaining human oversight"; research and scholarship rule, P62.
units.anchor: improve idea development, content structuring, and research design while maintaining human oversight

units.why: "Ensure that AI platforms have adequate data privacy measures and do not use inputted data to train publicly accessible models"; P50.
units.anchor: do not use inputted data to train publicly accessible models

units.why: Research bullet: consider risks of AI content to participants "and include notification in informed consent documents"; research rule, P62.
units.anchor: include notification in informed consent documents

units.why: "Know the publisher's requirements and limitations of AI use and disclosure before submitting content for publication"; defers to venue rules, P62.
units.anchor: Know the publisher

units.why: "Acquire training data ethically, respecting consent and privacy regulations"; research, P62.
units.anchor: Acquire training data ethically, respecting consent and privacy regulations

units.why: Under Work: "Use generative AI to improve administrative processes and decision-making"; operational AI use, P76.
units.anchor: Use generative AI to improve administrative processes and decision-making

units.why: "Ensure data privacy and security when using AI tools in daily tasks"; P50.
units.anchor: Ensure data privacy and security when using AI tools in daily tasks

units.why: "Stay informed about the latest AI developments and best practices"; P102.
units.anchor: Stay informed about the latest AI developments and best practices

units.why: "AI literacy training is actively available for faculty, staff and students"; P70.
units.anchor: AI literacy training is actively available for faculty, staff and students

units.why: The university "provides comprehensive resources and support ... through workshops, tutorials, and dedicated help centers"; P70.
units.anchor: provides comprehensive resources and support for learning about and using generative AI through workshops, tutorials

units.why: Describes personalization benefits: "analyze student data to create tailored learning experiences"; P87.
units.anchor: AI-powered platforms can analyze student data to create tailored learning experiences

units.why: Intelligent tutoring systems can supplement instruction by "Simulating one-on-one tutoring sessions"; benefit statement, P87.
units.anchor: Simulating one-on-one tutoring sessions

units.why: "AI tools can assist faculty in developing course materials" e.g. generating outlines, presentations, translations; faculty use, P59.
units.anchor: AI tools can assist faculty in developing course materials

units.why: "Courses might use or require AI tools"; AI built into coursework, P79.
units.anchor: Courses might use or require AI tools

units.why: "Some assignments may be graded using AI tools" that assess multiple-choice and provide initial essay feedback; tells students AI grading may occur, nearest P47.
units.anchor: Some assignments may be graded using AI tools
units.fit_note: States that AI grading may occur; no commitment to disclose or limit it.

units.why: Students may have access to AI research assistants that summarize articles, generate citations and suggest sources; summaries as study aid, P14.
units.anchor: Summarizing academic articles

units.why: "Inform students when AI tools are being used in the course and how they will impact learning and assessment"; instructor disclosure, P47.
units.anchor: Inform students when AI tools are being used in the course and how

units.why: "Ensure that AI-assisted teaching does not compromise learning objectives"; ties AI use to objectives, P83.
units.anchor: Ensure that AI-assisted teaching does not compromise learning objectives

units.why: "Provide AI literacy training: Help students understand the capabilities and limitations of AI tools"; student AI literacy, P70.
units.anchor: Help students understand the capabilities and limitations of AI tools

units.why: "Use AI to enhance, not replace, instruction ... maintaining the essential role of human instruction"; instructor use of AI for teaching, P59.
units.anchor: Use AI to enhance, not replace, instruction

units.why: "Acknowledge AI contributions: Clearly state when AI tools have been used in the research process"; research disclosure, P62.
units.anchor: Clearly state when AI tools have been used in the research process

units.why: "Validate AI-generated content: Verify the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated data"; research, P62.
units.anchor: Verify the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated data, analyses, or conclusions

units.why: Faculty should defer to guidelines of professional organizations, venues or funders; P62.
units.anchor: Follow any AI-related guidelines or best practices established by professional organizations

units.why: "Stay informed about AI developments: Engage in professional development opportunities to learn about new AI tools"; faculty keep up, P102.
units.anchor: Engage in professional development opportunities to learn about new AI tools

units.why: Faculty are asked to "Participate in university-wide conversations about AI governance"; involvement in making policy, which no listed type covers.
units.anchor: Participate in university-wide conversations about AI governance, ethics, and implementation
units.uncovered_note: Faculty and staff are asked to take part in university-wide discussions that shape AI policy.

units.why: "Model responsible AI use: Demonstrate ethical and responsible use of AI in your own work and mentor colleagues and students"; modelling and mentoring, which no listed type covers.
units.anchor: Demonstrate ethical and responsible use of AI in your own work
units.uncovered_note: Faculty should model and mentor responsible AI use for colleagues and students.

units.why: "Advocate for AI literacy: Support efforts to integrate AI literacy into curricula"; curricular AI literacy, P70.
units.anchor: Support efforts to integrate AI literacy into curricula

units.why: Staff may use AI "to automate routine tasks, such as data entry, scheduling, and document processing"; operational use, P76.
units.anchor: automate routine tasks, such as data entry, scheduling, and document processing

units.why: Staff may use "AI-powered chatbots or virtual assistants" to answer inquiries; operational and student-service AI, P76.
units.anchor: Utilize AI-powered chatbots or virtual assistants to provide quick and accurate

units.why: "Adhere to data governance policies: Follow the university's data classification standards and privacy policies"; staff handling sensitive data, P50.
units.anchor: Follow the university

units.why: Staff must "Work with the Division of Technology Services to implement security controls based on data classification"; P50.
units.anchor: Work with the Division of Technology Services to implement security controls

units.why: "Conduct regular audits: Assess and audit AI systems regularly"; P98.
units.anchor: Assess and audit AI systems regularly to identify and address potential data privacy risks

units.why: "Maintain transparency: Inform relevant stakeholders about the use of AI in decision-making processes and provide opportunities for feedback and oversight"; people told when AI is used, P103.
units.anchor: Inform relevant stakeholders about the use of AI in decision-making processes

units.why: "Mitigate bias: Be aware of potential biases in AI algorithms and take steps to mitigate them, such as ... regular audits"; P98 (monitoring for bias), not P53 since it prescribes action.
units.anchor: Be aware of potential biases in AI algorithms and take steps to mitigate them

units.why: "Ensure accessibility: Design AI-powered services and tools to be accessible to all users"; P97.
units.anchor: Design AI-powered services and tools to be accessible to all users

units.why: "Monitor outcomes: Regularly assess the impact of AI-driven decisions on different groups"; P98.
units.anchor: Regularly assess the impact of AI-driven decisions on different groups

units.why: "Participate in training: Attend workshops and tutorials"; staff training, P70.
units.anchor: Attend workshops and tutorials provided by the university to learn about AI

units.why: Student guidance: "Review the syllabus: Check for AI-related policies set by your instructor"; find each course's rule, P78.
units.anchor: Check for AI-related policies set by your instructor

units.why: "Ask for clarification: If AI usage is unclear, consult your professor"; P10.
units.anchor: If AI usage is unclear, consult your professor

units.why: "Follow academic integrity guidelines: Ensure compliance with Texas A&M University's academic policies"; comply with existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: Ensure compliance with Texas A&M University

units.why: "Brainstorm and generate ideas: Use Ai for inspiration, not as a final submission"; brainstorming, P15.
units.anchor: Use Ai for inspiration, not as a final submission
units.fit_note: Adds that AI output is not the final submission.

units.why: "Enhance your understanding: Leverage AI to clarify concepts, not as a replacement for studying"; tutor use, P12.
units.anchor: Leverage AI to clarify concepts, not as a replacement for studying

units.why: "Practice original thinking: Ensure that AI supports, rather than substitutes, your own work"; P32.
units.anchor: Ensure that AI supports, rather than substitutes, your own work

units.why: "Cross-check with academic sources: Validate AI-generated facts using credible materials"; P31.
units.anchor: Validate AI-generated facts using credible materials

units.why: "Be aware of biases and errors: AI may provide misleading or incorrect information"; AI is often wrong, P31.
units.anchor: AI may provide misleading or incorrect information

units.why: "Follow citations guidelines: Use the recommended format for AI-generated content"; P24.
units.anchor: Use the recommended format for AI-generated content

units.why: "Be transparent about AI use: Acknowledge AI assistance when used"; P24.
units.anchor: Acknowledge AI assistance when used

units.why: "Check with your instructor: Ensure AI citations align with course expectations"; ask instructor, P10.
units.anchor: Ensure AI citations align with course expectations

units.why: "Engage with university resources: Attend workshops or read AI-related guides"; student AI literacy, P70.
units.anchor: Attend workshops or read AI-related guides

units.why: "Consider ethical implications: Think about fairness, bias, and responsible AI use"; P53.
units.anchor: Think about fairness, bias, and responsible AI use

units.why: "Use university-approved tools: Prioritize AI tools vetted by Texas A&M University"; P92.
units.anchor: Prioritize AI tools vetted by Texas A&M University

units.why: "Avoid sharing sensitive information: Do not input personal, confidential, or proprietary data"; P50.
units.anchor: Do not input personal, confidential, or proprietary data

units.why: "Be mindful of data storage: Understand how AI tools store and use your information"; P50.
units.anchor: Understand how AI tools store and use your information

units.why: FAQ 1: AI "can be used to develop hands-on learning experiences that promote programming, creativity, and problem-solving skills"; benefit, P87.
units.anchor: develop hands-on learning experiences that promote programming, creativity, and problem-solving skills

units.why: FAQ 4: "Students can engage in various generative AI projects"; AI use is welcomed, P02.
units.anchor: Students can engage in various generative AI projects, such as creating generative art, music, chatbots

units.why: FAQ 3: AI can help faculty by "automating repetitive tasks, summarizing complex information, providing instant feedback to students"; faculty use, P59.
units.anchor: providing instant feedback to students

units.why: FAQ 5: "Sensitive information should not be entered into generative AI tools unless a risk assessment has been conducted, and the tool has been approved"; P50.
units.anchor: Sensitive information should not be entered into generative AI tools unless a risk assessment

units.why: FAQ 5: AI outputs "may raise complex copyright questions"; P52.
units.anchor: outputs generated by AI may raise complex copyright questions

units.why: FAQ 5: "avoid unintentional copyright violations by documenting the information being used by the various AI tools"; P52.
units.anchor: avoid unintentional copyright violations by

units.why: FAQ 6: staff disclose AI use for tasks affecting decisions or with ethical or legal implications; staff operational use, P76.
units.anchor: Staff should disclose the use of generative AI when it is used for tasks
units.fit_note: Staff disclosure of AI use in their work, not to students.

units.why: FAQ 6: "disclosure is not necessary for minor tasks or when significant edits are made"; staff disclosure exemption, P76.
units.anchor: disclosure is not necessary for minor tasks or when significant edits are made

units.why: FAQ 7: "professors can require students to use generative AI tools for assignments, but with certain restrictions"; P79.
units.anchor: professors can require students to use generative AI tools

units.why: FAQ 7: professors should "not require students to create accounts with non-university AI tools that require sharing personal information"; P51.
units.anchor: not require students to create accounts with non-university AI tools
units.fit_note: Frames the limit as personal-information sharing, not cost.

units.why: FAQ 7: professors "should encourage the use of university-approved AI tools"; P92.
units.anchor: should encourage the use of university-approved AI tools

units.why: FAQ 8: submitting AI work "as one's own without proper acknowledgment constitutes cheating"; misconduct, P36 (also non-acknowledgment).
units.anchor: as one's own without proper acknowledgment constitutes cheating and violates academic integrity policies

units.why: FAQ 9: faculty deter misuse by "designing assignments that focus on the process rather than the product"; P35.
units.anchor: designing assignments that focus on the process rather than the product

units.why: FAQ 9: faculty "should be using examples not found in AI training data"; P35.
units.anchor: using examples not found in AI training data

units.why: FAQ 9: faculty "require students to present their work and discuss their methods"; P34.
units.anchor: students to present their work and discuss their methods

units.why: FAQ 9: "incorporate low-stakes assignments and formative feedback throughout the course"; P35.
units.anchor: low-stakes assignments and formative feedback throughout the course

units.why: "Approved AI for Aggies: Prioritize the use of AI tools officially sanctioned by Texas A&M"; P92.
units.anchor: Prioritize the use of AI tools officially sanctioned by Texas A&M

units.why: "Keep up-to-date with evolving AI technologies and ethics. Participate in training sessions"; P102.
